# EAA update watcher pilot

Read [shared workflow](../workflow.md), [evidence](../evidence.md) and [review](../review.md). Those own evidence, budgets and publication gates. This file owns source selection, comparisons, scheduling and state. Cross-page research handoffs are required; public edits remain within authorised scope.

## Scope and ownership

Use only `erikgustafsson/en-301-549-resources-and-eaa-monitoring-testing` for branches, state and draft PRs. Pilot countries: Denmark and Sweden (established routes), Ireland, Italy and Portugal (known authorities with reporting gaps). Other countries and pages require a separate request. The next-country merge automation is disabled; merging a PR never authorizes a new country.

The assistant scheduler runs the pilot on Friday mornings in Europe/Stockholm. No GitHub Actions workflow is added. The first run of each calendar month also starts discovery; unfinished discovery resumes on later weekly runs. Initial discovery is incomplete as documented in `baseline-report.md`.

`inventory.json` contains every unique source URL in the five records at initialization, plus discovered leads. Claim indices refer to the recorded blob SHA; reload current records on each run, remap changed indices and register new source URLs without losing source IDs or history. Do not reuse an ID for a different URL. Preserve query parameters (official law URLs use them to select articles).

## Baseline and comparisons

The checked-in `baseline-observations.json` records the initial bounded reader pass. It is a partial baseline, not a new country audit. Each URL has a separate access result. Pending URLs have never been checked by this watcher. A readable page is not proof of usable intake, accepted language, completeness or a new event. Search crawl dates are not publication or effective dates.

State lives at `.github/agents/watcher/state.json` on the dedicated `watcher/pilot-state` branch of the testing repository. That branch is operational state only and must never be merged into main or the original repository. It stores observations, fingerprints, pending leads, monthly discovery progress, run history and review decisions. Initial state is seeded from the observations; `baseline-state.json` preserves that seed for review. No country assertions are changed by the state helper.

The runner observes official pages using available readers and, where authorized and necessary, an ordinary browser. `state.py` compares structured factual observations supplied by the runner. It does not crawl websites, automatically extract semantic facts or judge legal meaning. Keep field names and wording stable when content is unchanged. Compare prior facts and the original source in its language; ignore navigation, cookie notices, counters and styling. Preserve negation, numbers, dates, sector, audience, purpose, qualification and destination. Do not hash whole pages or translated free-form summaries as proof of a material change. Hash differences produce review candidates only.

Keep concise source sections, paraphrases, access date, reader method and freshness limits with observations. Do not store entire fetched pages, credentials, private correspondence or submitted personal data. Never carry error-page text into a last-good factual baseline.

## Each scheduled run

1. Read current main instructions and pilot country records, then open PRs and branches. If this infrastructure is not yet merged, use its known pilot branch for infrastructure instructions only; country update branches still start from current main. Do not fall back to a different repository.
2. Read the state file and its blob SHA. Acquire a 45-minute lease by updating that file with `lease: {owner: <unique run id>, expires_at: <UTC timestamp>}` using that exact SHA. On conflict or an unexpired foreign lease, stop without writing or creating PRs. After expiry a later run may take over. Before every write or PR operation, reread and verify ownership; never clear another run's lease. Release your own lease on completion. Do not start writes if state cannot be read.
3. Check all `weekly` sources and up to two `rotation` URLs per country, selecting never-checked then oldest-checked first. If a core source cannot be checked within the budget, explicitly record it as deferred. Inspect relevant linked reporting pages without submission. At most two attempts per failing destination in a run, including at most one ordinary-browser attempt; follow browser authorization rules. A search snippet is only a lead. TLS, robots, 403, session errors and login gates must be recorded accurately, without circumvention.
4. For monthly discovery, search the official domains and news/guidance sections in each country's language, using inventory terms and the record's unresolved questions. Read the actual official result before concluding. Cover authority changes, publication duties, non-compliance and exemptions, new intake, languages and relevant supervision announcements. Search for both recent news and undated guidance; use a lookback overlapping the last successful discovery by seven days. At initialization, search existing guidance without claiming it is newly published. If results are irrelevant or access is blocked, mark discovery partial and record the next useful query/page. Record progress per country and mark a month complete only after all five passes are completed. A complete bounded pass is not proof that no other news exists.
5. Run `state.py` on the latest state and the observations. Use one stable run ID for retries. Only `reachable` observations with substantive facts may establish a baseline. A first observation cannot prove a change since yesterday. Compare it with the country record to identify previously unknown evidence; add a distinct `discovery_candidate` event for such a lead, with source URL, section, publication date if available, and impacted claim/question. Register discovered URLs first. Keep earlier pending candidates until explicitly resolved, even if later checks are unchanged.
6. Review each candidate against current main, open/closed PRs and existing event decisions. Verify authority, jurisdiction, sector, audience, purpose, requirements versus recommendations, proposal versus enacted law, and effective date. Preserve correspondence facts and existing Yes/No unless explicit official evidence contradicts them. An inaccessible source does not disprove a fact. A query email does not establish statutory filing. Do not infer reporting languages from a translated website. Do not use public-sector WAD statements as EAA proof.
7. Propose only supported changes, using the existing research, verification, presentation, isolated language and targeted validation process. Use one-country draft PRs titled `Audit <country> EAA authorities and reporting routes`; add event IDs in the body. Keep at most one country research PR open and queue other candidates in state. Recheck open PRs, pending branches and main immediately before creating a branch/PR. If a country branch already has work, queue rather than overwrite it. An unrelated page PR does not block this pilot unless it changes a shared file. Never merge, enable auto-merge, write main, send correspondence or broaden public edits beyond authorised scope, change workflows or alter the calendar date script.
8. Commit state observations using the current blob SHA only on `watcher/pilot-state`. Record decision (`pending`, `needs_evidence`, `no_material_change`, `queued`, `draft_pr`, `merged`, `rejected`), rationale, PR reference and notification date against event IDs. Follow up pending review items even when hashes are unchanged. Do not replace a pending candidate with a false resolved status. A PR must be verified merged into main before recording it as merged.
9. Notify in ChatGPT for verified material findings, a new draft PR, or a persistent actionable blocker; stay quiet otherwise. An access failure becomes persistent after two separate runs, not two attempts in one run. Group repeated failures by destination/incident and suppress duplicate notifications. Never announce successful verification or a new rule based only on a hash, search snippet, reader-cache date or proposal. Record failed checks even when no notification is warranted.

Apply shared research limits; preserve progress and resume deferred work on the next authorised run. Do not expand the pilot or disable it on transient errors. State writes are confined to the operational branch; infrastructure changes require their own draft PR.

## Local usage and validation

`python3 .github/agents/watcher/state.py inventory.json previous-state.json observations.json` prints updated JSON without writing files. Use the full paths or run from this folder. Pass a non-existent previous-state path for initialization. Save the output with the approved file-edit tool, then validate before pushing.

`python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/agents/watcher -p 'test_*.py'` checks duplicate runs, whitespace noise, changed negation/deadlines, failure preservation, persistent failures, recovery, redirects, and unknown-to-known candidates. These are synthetic regression tests, not evidence that live detection has perfect recall.

For pilot assessment, record attempted/total sources, fresh versus cached access, deferred sources, relevant/irrelevant candidates, confirmed discoveries, repeated alerts and time spent. Missed changes are unknown without a comparison review: once monthly, have the maintainer compare an independent sample of five official pages/news sections with recorded candidates, and log any omissions. Move to the original repository only after explicit maintainer approval following at least three weekly runs and one monthly discovery cycle. Review candidate accuracy, coverage and unresolved access blockers; no automatic promotion threshold is implied.

## Concurrent projects

Other pages can be edited in separate branches and PRs. Watcher infrastructure is confined to `.github/agents/watcher/` plus explicitly required shared-instruction edits. Country updates touch only the relevant record and row. Before publication, inspect whether another PR touches any same file and refresh from main; never force-push, overwrite another project's branch or resolve conflicts by dropping its changes.
